The *Gotamivatthadānapañha* ("Why Should Gifts Be Given To the Order Rather Than To the Buddha?", Mil 6.1.2) is a section of the *Milindapañha* belonging to the late canonical or paracanonical Pali strata [SuttaCentral]. The text addresses the dilemma regarding the propriety and merit of offering gifts to the monastic community (*saṅgha*) as opposed to the Buddha directly, a discussion intimately linked with the episode of Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī offering a pair of cloths [SuttaCentral].

According to SuttaCentral, the doctrinal issue treated here relates directly to the *Dakkhiṇāvibhaṅga Sutta* (MN 142) and the *Kathāvatthu* (*Navattabbaṁsaṁghassadinnaṁmahapphalantikathā*, Kv 17.9) [SuttaCentral]. It also shares themes and references with MN 3, SN 2.30, AN 1.170, and Mil 6.4.2, alongside multiple Chinese and Tibetan parallels and discussions, including the Madhyama Āgama (MĀ 180), the *Fenbie bushi jing* (分別布施經, T 84), the *Dazhidulun* (T 1509.22), the *Abhidharma-mahāvibhāṣā* (T 1545.178), and narrative collections (T 202.52, T 203.50, T 212.14) [SuttaCentral].

Text-reuse computations by DharmaNexus reveal 225 matching passages across 28 Pali works [DharmaNexus]. It shares substantial passages with the canonical *Dakkhiṇāvibhaṅga Sutta* (MN 142, §3.3–4.1 matching §2.5–2.7 with high similarity), confirming the close relationship noted by SuttaCentral [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral]. Further prominent Pali reuse occurs with the *Ekakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 1), the *Majjhimanikāye Uparipaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā*, other questions within the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.3.2, Mil 5.2.5, Mil 6.1.5), the *Bahujanahita Sutta* (Iti 84), the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 17.9), and the *Milindaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matching, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of this text with the Chinese *Fenbie bushi jing* (T 84), supporting SuttaCentral's curated identification, and detects minor shared segments with the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral].
